title: Europe Explorer
description: Hop across Europe from London landmarks to Prague castles.
shortTagline: Capital cities, canals, and old town streets.

stops.name: London
stops.description: Start beside the Thames and historic landmarks.
stops.fact: London has more than 170 museums.

stops.name: Dover
stops.description: White cliffs mark the final English stop before the Channel.
stops.fact: Dover Castle has guarded the narrowest part of the Channel for centuries.

stops.name: Calais
stops.description: Arrive in France beside the Channel and its historic harbor.
stops.fact: On clear days the cliffs of Dover can be seen from Calais.

stops.name: Paris
stops.description: Boulevards, bridges, cafes, and the Eiffel Tower.
stops.fact: The Eiffel Tower can grow taller in hot weather.

stops.name: Lille
stops.description: Discover Flemish facades, lively squares, and northern French culture.
stops.fact: Lille was once one of the great merchant cities of Flanders.

stops.name: Brussels
stops.description: A compact capital full of squares and chocolate.
stops.fact: Brussels is famous for more than 180 nationalities.

stops.name: Antwerp
stops.description: Pause among guild houses, art, and a working river port.
stops.fact: Antwerp has been a major diamond-trading center for centuries.

stops.name: Rotterdam
stops.description: Modern architecture rises around one of Europe’s busiest ports.
stops.fact: Rotterdam rebuilt with bold modern design after World War II.

stops.name: Amsterdam
stops.description: Canals, bikes, narrow houses, and bright water.
stops.fact: Amsterdam has more bikes than residents.

stops.name: Hannover
stops.description: Green parks and red-brick streets break up the journey east.
stops.fact: Hannover’s Eilenriede is one of Europe’s largest urban forests.

stops.name: Berlin
stops.description: A creative capital with layered history.
stops.fact: Berlin has more bridges than Venice.

stops.name: Prague
stops.description: Finish among castle views and old town streets.
stops.fact: Prague Castle is one of the largest castle complexes on Earth.

title: Italy Dream
description: Walk Italy from Milan style to the warm streets of Naples.
shortTagline: Art, canals, ruins, and coastal flavor.

stops.name: Milan
stops.description: Fashion, design, and cathedral spires.
stops.fact: Milan Cathedral took nearly six centuries to complete.

stops.name: Bergamo
stops.description: Climb into a walled upper city of stone lanes and broad views.
stops.fact: Bergamo’s Venetian Walls are part of a UNESCO World Heritage site.

stops.name: Brescia
stops.description: Roman ruins and graceful squares mark the road east.
stops.fact: Brescia preserves one of northern Italy’s largest Roman archaeological areas.

stops.name: Verona
stops.description: Walk beside the Adige through Roman gates and medieval streets.
stops.fact: Verona’s Roman arena has hosted public events for nearly two thousand years.

stops.name: Padua
stops.description: Arcaded streets lead to frescoes, markets, and a vast elliptical square.
stops.fact: The University of Padua was founded in 1222.

stops.name: Venice
stops.description: A floating maze of canals and bridges.
stops.fact: Venice is built on more than 100 small islands.

stops.name: Ferrara
stops.description: Renaissance walls, bicycles, and a moated castle shape this quiet stop.
stops.fact: Ferrara was one of Europe’s earliest cities planned with modern urban principles.

stops.name: Bologna
stops.description: Long porticoes shelter a city of towers, markets, and rich food traditions.
stops.fact: Bologna’s historic porticoes extend for more than 60 kilometers.

stops.name: Florence
stops.description: Renaissance art wrapped in Tuscan light.
stops.fact: Florence was once the capital of Italy.

stops.name: Siena
stops.description: Brick lanes converge on a shell-shaped piazza in the Tuscan hills.
stops.fact: Siena’s Palio horse race has roots stretching back to the seventeenth century.

stops.name: Orvieto
stops.description: A dramatic volcanic plateau carries a striped cathedral above the valley.
stops.fact: Orvieto sits on a mass of volcanic tuff above caves carved over many centuries.

stops.name: Rome
stops.description: Ancient ruins, fountains, and endless streets.
stops.fact: Rome has a sovereign country inside it: Vatican City.

stops.name: Cassino
stops.description: The route passes beneath a rebuilt hilltop abbey with a long history.
stops.fact: Monte Cassino Abbey was founded by Benedict of Nursia around 529.

stops.name: Naples
stops.description: A lively finish near the bay and Vesuvius.
stops.fact: Naples is often called the birthplace of pizza.

title: Japan Tour
description: Trace Japan from Tokyo energy to Kyoto calm and Hiroshima.
shortTagline: Neon cities, temples, mountains, and peace parks.

stops.name: Tokyo
stops.description: A neon start with temples tucked between towers.
stops.fact: Tokyo is one of the world's most populous metro areas.

stops.name: Yokohama
stops.description: A waterfront skyline and historic port open the road south.
stops.fact: Yokohama developed rapidly after its port opened to international trade in 1859.

stops.name: Hakone
stops.description: Hot springs and mountain views near Fuji.
stops.fact: Hakone is known for black eggs boiled in volcanic springs.

stops.name: Shizuoka
stops.description: Tea country and views of Mount Fuji accompany the journey west.
stops.fact: Shizuoka Prefecture is one of Japan’s leading tea-producing regions.

stops.name: Hamamatsu
stops.description: Lakeside landscapes meet a city known for music and engineering.
stops.fact: Major Japanese musical-instrument companies were founded in Hamamatsu.

stops.name: Nagoya
stops.description: A castle city blends samurai history with modern industry.
stops.fact: Nagoya Castle is famous for the golden shachihoko on its roof.

stops.name: Kyoto
stops.description: Shrines, bamboo groves, and old lanes.
stops.fact: Kyoto has more than 1,600 Buddhist temples.

stops.name: Osaka
stops.description: Street food, castles, and bright nightlife.
stops.fact: Osaka is nicknamed Japan's kitchen.

stops.name: Kobe
stops.description: Mountain slopes descend toward a cosmopolitan harbor.
stops.fact: Kobe was among the first Japanese ports opened to international trade in the nineteenth century.

stops.name: Himeji
stops.description: A brilliant white castle rises above gardens and old streets.
stops.fact: Himeji Castle is Japan’s largest surviving feudal castle complex.

stops.name: Okayama
stops.description: A celebrated landscape garden offers a calm stop beside the river.
stops.fact: Korakuen is traditionally counted among Japan’s three great gardens.

stops.name: Fukuyama
stops.description: A castle town leads toward the historic ports of the Seto Inland Sea.
stops.fact: Nearby Tomonoura has served as a sheltered port for more than a thousand years.

stops.name: Hiroshima
stops.description: A meaningful final stop by Peace Memorial Park.
stops.fact: Hiroshima rebuilt its streetcar network after World War II.

title: Route 66 USA
description: Follow the spirit of Route 66 from Chicago to Los Angeles.
shortTagline: Classic diners, desert towns, and Pacific dreams.

stops.name: Chicago
stops.description: Begin near Lake Michigan and classic diners.
stops.fact: Route 66 originally began in Chicago in 1926.

stops.name: Joliet
stops.description: Historic road signs and limestone landmarks welcome travelers out of Chicago.
stops.fact: Joliet’s former prison is one of the best-known landmarks along Illinois Route 66.

stops.name: Springfield, Illinois
stops.description: Lincoln history and classic roadside stops anchor the Illinois stretch.
stops.fact: Springfield contains Abraham Lincoln’s home and presidential museum.

stops.name: St. Louis
stops.description: Pass the Gateway Arch on the Mississippi.
stops.fact: The Gateway Arch is 630 feet tall and 630 feet wide.

stops.name: Springfield, Missouri
stops.description: Neon signs and roadside history mark the birthplace of the route’s famous name.
stops.fact: A 1926 telegram sent from Springfield helped establish the name Route 66.

stops.name: Joplin
stops.description: Murals and mining history accompany the road toward Oklahoma.
stops.fact: Joplin grew rapidly during the regional lead and zinc mining boom.

stops.name: Tulsa
stops.description: Art deco details and road-trip history.
stops.fact: Tulsa calls itself the capital of Route 66.

stops.name: Oklahoma City
stops.description: The route crosses a state capital filled with western and road-trip history.
stops.fact: Oklahoma has more drivable miles of historic Route 66 than any other state.

stops.name: Amarillo
stops.description: Big skies, cattle culture, and roadside art define the Texas Panhandle.
stops.fact: Cadillac Ranch has displayed its line of buried cars west of Amarillo since 1974.

stops.name: Tucumcari
stops.description: Restored neon motels preserve the atmosphere of the Mother Road.
stops.fact: Tucumcari Boulevard retains a notable collection of Route 66 neon signs.

stops.name: Santa Fe
stops.description: Desert colors, adobe architecture, and big sky.
stops.fact: Santa Fe is the oldest state capital in the United States.

stops.name: Albuquerque
stops.description: Adobe neighborhoods and vintage signs follow the Rio Grande valley.
stops.fact: Central Avenue carries Route 66 through the heart of Albuquerque.

stops.name: Gallup
stops.description: Red-rock country surrounds a trading town rich in Native American culture.
stops.fact: Gallup has long been a regional center for Native arts and trading posts.

stops.name: Winslow
stops.description: Railroad heritage and a famous downtown corner enliven the Arizona road.
stops.fact: Winslow grew as an important stop on the Santa Fe Railway.

stops.name: Flagstaff
stops.description: Pine forest and mountain air replace the open desert.
stops.fact: Flagstaff became the world’s first International Dark Sky City in 2001.

stops.name: Kingman
stops.description: A historic depot introduces one of Arizona’s best-preserved Route 66 stretches.
stops.fact: Kingman sits beside a long driveable section of historic Route 66 through northwestern Arizona.

stops.name: Barstow
stops.description: Desert rail history and roadside museums signal the approach to California’s coast.
stops.fact: Barstow stands at a major historic junction of Route 66 and rail lines.

stops.name: San Bernardino
stops.description: The road leaves the Mojave behind and enters Southern California’s urban basin.
stops.fact: San Bernardino is home to the site of the first McDonald’s restaurant.

stops.name: Los Angeles
stops.description: Finish by the Pacific after a long virtual trek.
stops.fact: Historic Route 66 ended near Santa Monica Pier.

title: Nordic Route
description: Explore Nordic capitals and calm coastal landscapes.
shortTagline: Harbors, islands, fjords, and northern design.

stops.name: Copenhagen
stops.description: Start with harbors, bikes, and colorful facades.
stops.fact: Copenhagen has more bicycles than cars.

stops.name: Malmö
stops.description: Cross the Öresund into a waterfront city of old squares and bold modern design.
stops.fact: The Öresund Bridge carries both road and rail traffic between Denmark and Sweden.

stops.name: Jönköping
stops.description: Pause beside Lake Vättern among lakeside paths, museums, and match-manufacturing history.
stops.fact: Jönköping sits at the southern end of Lake Vättern, Sweden’s second-largest lake.

stops.name: Stockholm
stops.description: An island capital built across water.
stops.fact: Stockholm spreads across 14 islands.

stops.name: Örebro
stops.description: Follow the Svartån River past a medieval castle and wooden historic quarter.
stops.fact: Örebro Castle has stood at this river crossing for roughly seven centuries.

stops.name: Karlstad
stops.description: Meet the Klarälven River near Lake Vänern in Sweden’s sunny city.
stops.fact: Karlstad stands where Sweden’s longest river reaches Vänern, the European Union’s largest lake.

stops.name: Oslo
stops.description: Green hills, fjord views, and modern museums.
stops.fact: Most of Oslo is forest or green space.

stops.name: Turku
stops.description: Arrive on the Aura River among medieval landmarks and Baltic maritime history.
stops.fact: Turku Cathedral was consecrated in 1300 and is Finland’s national shrine.

stops.name: Helsinki
stops.description: A Baltic finish with design and sea air.
stops.fact: Helsinki has hundreds of islands in its archipelago.

title: Camino de Santiago
description: Walk a Camino-inspired route toward Santiago de Compostela.
shortTagline: Pilgrim towns, cathedrals, and quiet roads.

stops.name: Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port
stops.description: A mountain village at the traditional Camino start.
stops.fact: The town name means Saint John at the foot of the pass.

stops.name: Pamplona
stops.description: Medieval streets and lively plazas.
stops.fact: Pamplona is famous for the San Fermin festival.

stops.name: Logrono
stops.description: A Rioja capital where the Camino crosses the Ebro beside old churches and lively tapas streets.
stops.fact: Logrono is mentioned in the 12th-century Codex Calixtinus, an early guide to the Camino.

stops.name: Burgos
stops.description: A cathedral city with Gothic drama.
stops.fact: Burgos Cathedral is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

stops.name: Fromista
stops.description: A compact Castilian stop of Romanesque stone, canal water, and open meseta landscapes.
stops.fact: The Church of San Martin is one of the best-known Romanesque landmarks on the French Way.

stops.name: Leon
stops.description: Stained glass, old walls, and pilgrim energy.
stops.fact: Leon Cathedral is nicknamed the House of Light.

stops.name: Astorga
stops.description: Roman heritage and Gaudi architecture meet where two historic pilgrimage routes cross.
stops.fact: Gaudi designed Astorga Episcopal Palace in a distinctive neo-Gothic style.

stops.name: Ponferrada
stops.description: A Bierzo valley city dominated by a many-towered Templar castle.
stops.fact: The Castle of the Templars guards a historic crossing of the Sil River.

stops.name: Sarria
stops.description: A green Galician Camino town and the most popular starting point for the final walk to Santiago.
stops.fact: Sarria lies just beyond the minimum 100-kilometre walking distance required for the Compostela certificate.

stops.name: Santiago de Compostela
stops.description: The classic finish at the cathedral square.
stops.fact: Pilgrims have walked to Santiago for more than 1,000 years.

title: Silk Road Journey
description: Join a virtual caravan across great Silk Road cities.
shortTagline: Trading cities, blue domes, and desert crossings.

stops.name: Istanbul
stops.description: A bridge between continents and cultures.
stops.fact: Istanbul has been capital of three major empires.

stops.name: Ankara
stops.description: An Anatolian capital layered with a Roman temple, a hilltop citadel, and modern museums.
stops.fact: Ankara became the capital of the Republic of Turkey in 1923.

stops.name: Goreme
stops.description: A Cappadocian settlement surrounded by volcanic valleys, cave churches, and rock-cut homes.
stops.fact: The Goreme Open-Air Museum preserves a major complex of medieval rock-cut churches.

stops.name: Tabriz
stops.description: A historic Iranian trading city centered on one of the Silk Road's great covered bazaars.
stops.fact: The Tabriz Historic Bazaar Complex is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

stops.name: Tehran
stops.description: A mountain-framed capital with deep history.
stops.fact: Tehran sits near the Alborz Mountains.

stops.name: Mashhad
stops.description: A major Khorasan city shaped by pilgrimage, poetry, bazaars, and routes toward Central Asia.
stops.fact: Mashhad grew around the shrine of Imam Reza, one of the world's largest mosque complexes.

stops.name: Bukhara
stops.description: An oasis city of blue domes, brick minarets, trading halls, and preserved caravan history.
stops.fact: Bukhara served for centuries as a major center of trade and Islamic learning.

stops.name: Samarkand
stops.description: Blue domes and caravanserai memories.
stops.fact: Samarkand was a key Silk Road crossroads.

stops.name: Tashkent
stops.description: A leafy Central Asian capital where old mahallas and markets meet monumental modern avenues.
stops.fact: Tashkent has long connected the settled oases of Transoxiana with routes toward the Tian Shan.

stops.name: Osh
stops.description: A Fergana Valley market city beneath sacred Sulayman Mountain.
stops.fact: Osh has served travelers and traders on Central Asian routes for more than two millennia.

stops.name: Kashgar
stops.description: Markets, desert routes, and old trading paths.
stops.fact: Kashgar has been a trading hub for over two millennia.

stops.name: Turpan
stops.description: A desert oasis of vineyards, ancient ruins, and underground irrigation north of the Taklamakan.
stops.fact: Turpan's karez channels carry mountain water underground to fields in the arid basin.

stops.name: Dunhuang
stops.description: A Gansu Corridor oasis known for painted caves, dunes, and caravan-route archaeology.
stops.fact: The Mogao Caves preserve nearly a thousand years of Buddhist art beside the Silk Roads.

stops.name: Xian
stops.description: End near ancient walls and terracotta warriors.
stops.fact: Xian was the eastern starting point of the Silk Road.

title: Ancient Egypt
description: Follow the Nile from Cairo to ancient southern temples.
shortTagline: Pyramids, Nile cities, temples, and desert light.

stops.name: Cairo
stops.description: Begin near the Nile and the pyramids.
stops.fact: Cairo is one of the largest cities in Africa.

stops.name: Giza
stops.description: Walk toward the last ancient wonder still standing.
stops.fact: The Great Pyramid was the tallest human-made structure for millennia.

stops.name: Saqqara
stops.description: A vast desert necropolis where royal tombs trace the development of pyramid building.
stops.fact: Djoser's Step Pyramid is the oldest monumental stone pyramid in Egypt.

stops.name: Minya
stops.description: A Nile city near limestone cliffs, ancient tombs, and the ruins of Akhenaten's capital.
stops.fact: Nearby Tell el-Amarna was founded as the royal city Akhetaten in the 14th century BCE.

stops.name: Abydos
stops.description: A sacred Upper Egyptian site associated with Osiris and the earliest pharaohs.
stops.fact: The Temple of Seti I contains the Abydos King List of earlier Egyptian rulers.

stops.name: Luxor
stops.description: Open-air history among temples and tombs.
stops.fact: Luxor is often called the world's greatest open-air museum.

stops.name: Edfu
stops.description: A riverside town centered on one of Egypt's most complete ancient temples.
stops.fact: The Temple of Horus at Edfu was built mainly during the Ptolemaic period.

stops.name: Kom Ombo
stops.description: A Nile bend where a rare double temple overlooks the river and cultivated fields.
stops.fact: Kom Ombo Temple has twin sanctuaries dedicated to Sobek and Horus the Elder.

stops.name: Aswan
stops.description: A calm southern finish by islands and desert.
stops.fact: Aswan was an ancient gateway to Nubia.

title: Australia Coast
description: Walk Australia’s east coast from Sydney to Cairns.
shortTagline: Harbors, surf towns, tropics, and reef gateways.

stops.name: Sydney
stops.description: Harbor views, beaches, and a bright coastal start.
stops.fact: The Sydney Opera House has over one million roof tiles.

stops.name: Newcastle
stops.description: Surf beaches and harbor history.
stops.fact: Newcastle is one of the world's largest coal export ports.

stops.name: Port Macquarie
stops.description: A Hastings River town of beaches, coastal rainforest, and important koala conservation work.
stops.fact: Port Macquarie was established as a British penal settlement in 1821.

stops.name: Coffs Harbour
stops.description: A subtropical coast stop of beaches, banana-growing history, and marine reserves.
stops.fact: The Big Banana opened in 1964 and became one of Australia's first famous Big Things.

stops.name: Byron Bay
stops.description: A surf town where rainforest hills meet beaches at mainland Australia's eastern edge.
stops.fact: Cape Byron is the easternmost point of mainland Australia.

stops.name: Brisbane
stops.description: River walks and warm subtropical air.
stops.fact: Brisbane gets more than 280 days of sunshine a year.

stops.name: Hervey Bay
stops.description: A sheltered coastal city known for whale watching and access to K'gari.
stops.fact: The calm waters of Hervey Bay are an important resting area for migrating humpback whales.

stops.name: Rockhampton
stops.description: A Fitzroy River city blending heritage streets, tropical gardens, and cattle-country culture.
stops.fact: The Tropic of Capricorn passes just south of central Rockhampton.

stops.name: Airlie Beach
stops.description: A lively coastal gateway to the Whitsunday Islands and the Great Barrier Reef.
stops.fact: Airlie Beach faces the Whitsundays, an archipelago of 74 islands.

stops.name: Townsville
stops.description: A tropical gateway near Magnetic Island.
stops.fact: Magnetic Island has one of Australia's largest wild koala colonies.

stops.name: Mission Beach
stops.description: A tropical village corridor between rainforest, long beaches, and the Coral Sea.
stops.fact: The Mission Beach region is habitat for the endangered southern cassowary.

stops.name: Cairns
stops.description: Finish near rainforest and reef adventures.
stops.fact: Cairns is a gateway to the Great Barrier Reef.

title: Alps Journey
description: Cross scenic Alpine stops from Geneva to Munich.
shortTagline: Lakes, valleys, alpine towns, and mountain air.

stops.name: Geneva
stops.description: Lake views and mountain horizons.
stops.fact: Geneva has one of the world's tallest fountain jets.

stops.name: Lausanne
stops.description: A steep lakeside city of vineyards, medieval streets, and Olympic heritage.
stops.fact: Lausanne has hosted the International Olympic Committee since 1915.

stops.name: Bern
stops.description: Arcaded sandstone streets curl around an Aare River peninsula beneath Alpine views.
stops.fact: Bern's medieval old town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

stops.name: Interlaken
stops.description: A valley stop between two lakes.
stops.fact: Interlaken sits between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz.

stops.name: Lucerne
stops.description: A lake city of painted squares, wooden bridges, and mountain excursions.
stops.fact: The Chapel Bridge is one of Europe's oldest covered wooden bridges.

stops.name: Andermatt
stops.description: An Urseren Valley village ringed by high passes and the dramatic Schollenen Gorge.
stops.fact: The headwaters of the Rhine, Rhone, Reuss, and Ticino lie in the wider Gotthard region.

stops.name: St. Moritz
stops.description: An Engadin resort beside a high Alpine lake, known for winter sport and panoramic railways.
stops.fact: St. Moritz hosted the Winter Olympic Games in 1928 and 1948.

stops.name: Innsbruck
stops.description: Colorful facades beneath steep peaks.
stops.fact: Innsbruck hosted the Winter Olympics twice.

stops.name: Garmisch-Partenkirchen
stops.description: A Bavarian mountain town beneath the Zugspitze, with painted houses and deep gorges.
stops.fact: The nearby Zugspitze is Germany's highest mountain at 2,962 metres.

stops.name: Munich
stops.description: A Bavarian finish with parks and beer gardens.
stops.fact: Munich's English Garden is larger than Central Park.

title: Around Ukraine
description: Discover Ukraine through its capitals, coast, and culture.
shortTagline: Historic cities, Carpathian charm, and Black Sea light.

stops.name: Kyiv
stops.description: Begin among hills, domes, and the Dnipro River.
stops.fact: Kyiv is one of Eastern Europe's oldest cities.

stops.name: Zhytomyr
stops.description: A green riverside city shaped by space exploration and old trade routes.
stops.fact: Zhytomyr is the birthplace of rocket engineer Sergei Korolev.

stops.name: Rivne
stops.description: A compact Volhynian city of parks, museums, and amber traditions.
stops.fact: Rivne region contains major deposits of Ukrainian amber.

stops.name: Lviv
stops.description: Coffee houses, courtyards, and old town charm.
stops.fact: Lviv's historic center is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

stops.name: Ivano-Frankivsk
stops.description: A welcoming Carpathian gateway centered on a lively pedestrian old town.
stops.fact: The city was founded in the 17th century as Stanislawow.

stops.name: Mukachevo
stops.description: A Transcarpathian town watched over by hilltop Palanok Castle.
stops.fact: Palanok Castle rises on an ancient volcanic hill.

stops.name: Uzhhorod
stops.description: A compact Carpathian city near the border.
stops.fact: Uzhhorod is known for its spring cherry blossoms.

stops.name: Chernivtsi
stops.description: Bukovinian architecture, café culture, and a remarkable university ensemble.
stops.fact: The former Residence of Bukovinian Metropolitans is UNESCO-listed.

stops.name: Vinnytsia
stops.description: A Podillia city of river promenades, historic estates, and museums.
stops.fact: Vinnytsia stands on both banks of the Southern Bug River.

stops.name: Odesa
stops.description: Sea air, grand stairs, and sunny boulevards.
stops.fact: The Potemkin Stairs are one of Odesa's famous landmarks.

stops.name: Dnipro
stops.description: A major city of broad river views, engineering, and space history.
stops.fact: Dnipro became an important center of rocket and spacecraft engineering.

stops.name: Kharkiv
stops.description: A major cultural and university city.
stops.fact: Kharkiv was once the capital of Soviet Ukraine.

title: France Tour
description: Travel France from Paris elegance to Mediterranean sun.
shortTagline: Boulevards, wine regions, Provence, and Riviera blue.

stops.name: Paris
stops.description: Begin with bridges, museums, and grand avenues.
stops.fact: Paris has more than 450 parks and gardens.

stops.name: Fontainebleau
stops.description: A royal town beside a vast forest and centuries of palace architecture.
stops.fact: French rulers transformed Fontainebleau Palace across eight centuries.

stops.name: Auxerre
stops.description: A Burgundy river town of half-timbered lanes and church towers.
stops.fact: Auxerre overlooks the Yonne on a historic route toward Burgundy.

stops.name: Dijon
stops.description: Burgundy flavors and tiled rooftops.
stops.fact: Dijon is famous for mustard and wine country nearby.

stops.name: Beaune
stops.description: Burgundy wine heritage surrounds a beautifully tiled medieval hospice.
stops.fact: The Hospices de Beaune has held a famous charity wine auction since 1859.

stops.name: Lyon
stops.description: A food capital between two rivers.
stops.fact: Lyon has hidden passageways called traboules.

stops.name: Valence
stops.description: A Rhône Valley stop where southern light meets parks and canals.
stops.fact: Valence is often described as a gateway to the south of France.

stops.name: Avignon
stops.description: Medieval walls and papal palace views.
stops.fact: Avignon was once the seat of popes.

stops.name: Marseille
stops.description: An ancient Mediterranean port framed by islands and limestone calanques.
stops.fact: Marseille was founded by Greek settlers around 600 BCE.

stops.name: Toulon
stops.description: A Mediterranean naval city gathered around a sheltered harbor and steep hills.
stops.fact: Toulon has been one of France's principal naval bases for centuries.

stops.name: Cannes
stops.description: A Riviera city of old hillside lanes, beaches, and cinema history.
stops.fact: The Cannes Film Festival has been held in the city since 1946.

stops.name: Nice
stops.description: A Riviera finish by blue Mediterranean water.
stops.fact: Nice became part of France in 1860.

title: Spain Tour
description: Loop through Spain’s cities, coast, and warm plazas.
shortTagline: Royal plazas, flamenco, paella, and Gaudi curves.

stops.name: Madrid
stops.description: Start in the energetic heart of Spain.
stops.fact: Madrid is one of Europe's highest capital cities.

stops.name: Toledo
stops.description: A hilltop city of stone lanes and old walls.
stops.fact: Toledo is known as the City of Three Cultures.

stops.name: Merida
stops.description: A walkable city where Roman monuments line the Guadiana River.
stops.fact: Merida preserves one of Spain's finest Roman archaeological ensembles.

stops.name: Cordoba
stops.description: Patios, stone lanes, and layered cultures beside the Guadalquivir.
stops.fact: Cordoba's historic center is among Europe's largest UNESCO urban sites.

stops.name: Seville
stops.description: Orange trees, flamenco, and warm plazas.
stops.fact: Seville's cathedral is one of the largest Gothic cathedrals.

stops.name: Granada
stops.description: A dramatic Andalusian city beneath the Alhambra and Sierra Nevada.
stops.fact: The Alhambra began as a fortress and became a Nasrid royal city.

stops.name: Alicante
stops.description: A Mediterranean port beneath the rocky Santa Barbara Castle.
stops.fact: Alicante's patterned Explanada promenade uses millions of marble tiles.

stops.name: Valencia
stops.description: A coastal city of gardens and modern architecture.
stops.fact: Valencia is the birthplace of paella.

stops.name: Tarragona
stops.description: Roman ruins and Catalan streets rise above the Mediterranean.
stops.fact: Ancient Tarraco was the first major Roman base on the Iberian Peninsula.

stops.name: Barcelona
stops.description: Finish among Gaudi curves and Mediterranean light.
stops.fact: La Sagrada Familia has been under construction since 1882.

title: Great Britain Walk
description: Walk from London to Edinburgh through British highlights.
shortTagline: University towns, northern cities, and castle views.

stops.name: London
stops.description: Begin in the capital beside the Thames.
stops.fact: The London Underground opened in 1863.

stops.name: Oxford
stops.description: College courtyards and river paths.
stops.fact: Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire.

stops.name: Stratford-upon-Avon
stops.description: A riverside market town shaped by Shakespeare and Tudor architecture.
stops.fact: William Shakespeare was born and died in Stratford-upon-Avon.

stops.name: Birmingham
stops.description: Canals, industrial heritage, creative districts, and a renowned food scene.
stops.fact: Birmingham's Jewellery Quarter has produced jewelry for centuries.

stops.name: Manchester
stops.description: Music, industry, and red-brick streets.
stops.fact: Manchester helped drive the Industrial Revolution.

stops.name: York
stops.description: Ancient walls and medieval lanes.
stops.fact: York Minster has some of Europe's largest medieval stained glass.

stops.name: Durham
stops.description: A compact cathedral city wrapped around a wooded river peninsula.
stops.fact: Durham Cathedral and Castle form a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

stops.name: Newcastle upon Tyne
stops.description: A lively Tyne city known for bridges, engineering, and culture.
stops.fact: The Tyne Bridge opened in 1928 and became a symbol of the city.

stops.name: Alnwick
stops.description: A Northumberland market town dominated by a grand working castle.
stops.fact: Alnwick Castle has served as a screen location for film and television.

stops.name: Edinburgh
stops.description: A castle-topped finish with dramatic streets.
stops.fact: Edinburgh has more listed buildings than anywhere in the UK outside London.

title: Turkey Journey
description: Cross Turkey from Istanbul to Cappadocia and Antalya.
shortTagline: Two continents, fairy chimneys, and turquoise coast.

stops.name: Istanbul
stops.description: Begin between Europe and Asia.
stops.fact: Istanbul is the only city spanning two continents.

stops.name: Bursa
stops.description: An early Ottoman capital of green parks, markets, mosques, and thermal baths.
stops.fact: Bursa and nearby Cumalikizik are recognized together by UNESCO.

stops.name: Eskisehir
stops.description: A youthful Anatolian city with colorful Ottoman houses and river walks.
stops.fact: Eskisehir is famous for carving local meerschaum stone.

stops.name: Ankara
stops.description: A modern capital on the Anatolian plateau.
stops.fact: Ankara became Turkey's capital in 1923.

stops.name: Hattusa
stops.description: Monumental gates and stone walls mark the Hittite imperial capital.
stops.fact: Thousands of cuneiform tablets found at Hattusa included ancient treaties.

stops.name: Cappadocia
stops.description: Fairy chimneys and sunrise balloons.
stops.fact: Cappadocia has ancient underground cities.

stops.name: Konya
stops.description: A Seljuk city of turquoise tiles, spiritual heritage, and broad squares.
stops.fact: Konya is closely associated with the poet and mystic Rumi.

stops.name: Side
stops.description: Ancient columns and a seaside theater meet beaches on a small peninsula.
stops.fact: Side was an important ancient port of Pamphylia.

stops.name: Antalya
stops.description: Finish by cliffs and turquoise water.
stops.fact: Antalya is known as the gateway to the Turkish Riviera.

title: Balkan Route
description: Move through the Balkans from Zagreb to Thessaloniki.
shortTagline: Layered capitals, river forts, and seaside history.

stops.name: Zagreb
stops.description: A graceful start of trams and cafe streets.
stops.fact: Zagreb has one of the shortest funiculars in the world.

stops.name: Banja Luka
stops.description: A green riverside city of boulevards, fortifications, and thermal traditions.
stops.fact: The Vrbas River runs through the center of Banja Luka.

stops.name: Sarajevo
stops.description: A city where cultures meet in narrow streets.
stops.fact: Sarajevo hosted the 1984 Winter Olympics.

stops.name: Tuzla
stops.description: A lively city built around salt heritage and unusual urban lakes.
stops.fact: Tuzla takes its name and much of its history from local salt deposits.

stops.name: Belgrade
stops.description: Rivers, fortress views, and late-night energy.
stops.fact: Belgrade sits where the Sava meets the Danube.

stops.name: Nis
stops.description: A southern Serbian crossroads with Roman heritage and an Ottoman fortress.
stops.fact: Roman emperor Constantine the Great was born in ancient Naissus.

stops.name: Sofia
stops.description: Mountain-backed boulevards and ancient layers.
stops.fact: Sofia is one of Europe's oldest capitals.

stops.name: Rila Monastery
stops.description: A mountain monastery of striped arcades, frescoes, and forested peaks.
stops.fact: Rila Monastery is Bulgaria's largest Eastern Orthodox monastery.

stops.name: Sandanski
stops.description: A warm spa town of parks and mineral springs near the Greek border.
stops.fact: Sandanski is named after Bulgarian revolutionary Yane Sandanski.

stops.name: Thessaloniki
stops.description: A seaside finish with Byzantine history.
stops.fact: Thessaloniki is known for its long waterfront promenade.

title: South America Explorer
description: Explore South America from Buenos Aires to Rio.
shortTagline: Tango streets, Andes views, Inca history, and beaches.

stops.name: Buenos Aires
stops.description: A tango-filled start of avenues and cafes.
stops.fact: Buenos Aires has one of the world's widest avenues.

stops.name: Cordoba Argentina
stops.description: A university city of Jesuit heritage, plazas, and nearby sierras.
stops.fact: The Jesuit Block of Cordoba is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

stops.name: Mendoza
stops.description: Tree-lined streets and vineyards rise beneath the eastern Andes.
stops.fact: Mendoza is the heart of Argentina's best-known wine region.

stops.name: Santiago
stops.description: A capital framed by the Andes.
stops.fact: Santiago sits in a valley surrounded by mountains.

stops.name: Antofagasta
stops.description: A Pacific port between the ocean and the immense Atacama Desert.
stops.fact: Antofagasta grew rapidly through the nitrate and copper industries.

stops.name: Arica
stops.description: A sunny northern port beneath the steep Morro de Arica.
stops.fact: Arica lies near the mouth of the fertile Azapa Valley.

stops.name: Arequipa
stops.description: A highland city of pale volcanic stone beneath dramatic volcanoes.
stops.fact: Arequipa's historic center is built largely from white sillar stone.

stops.name: Cusco
stops.description: High-altitude streets and Inca foundations.
stops.fact: Cusco was the capital of the Inca Empire.

stops.name: Nazca
stops.description: A desert town near vast ancient geoglyphs and ingenious aqueducts.
stops.fact: The Nazca Lines were created across the desert over many centuries.

stops.name: Lima
stops.description: Clifftop ocean views and culinary fame.
stops.fact: Lima is one of the driest capital cities.

stops.name: Foz do Iguacu
stops.description: A border city beside one of the world's great waterfall systems.
stops.fact: Iguacu Falls spans the frontier between Brazil and Argentina.

stops.name: Sao Paulo
stops.description: A vast cultural and culinary metropolis of museums and neighborhoods.
stops.fact: Sao Paulo is the largest city in the Southern Hemisphere by population.

stops.name: Rio de Janeiro
stops.description: A dramatic finish of beaches and mountains.
stops.fact: Rio was once the capital of Portugal for a brief period.

title: Canada Route
description: Cross Canada from Montreal to Vancouver.
shortTagline: Great lakes, prairies, Rockies, and Pacific forests.

stops.name: Montreal
stops.description: A bilingual start of festivals and old stone streets.
stops.fact: Montreal is built around Mount Royal.

stops.name: Ottawa
stops.description: Canada's capital combines Gothic landmarks, museums, and river paths.
stops.fact: Ottawa became the capital of the Province of Canada in 1857.

stops.name: Kingston
stops.description: A limestone city where Lake Ontario meets the Saint Lawrence River.
stops.fact: Kingston briefly served as the first capital of the united Province of Canada.

stops.name: Toronto
stops.description: Skylines, neighborhoods, and Lake Ontario.
stops.fact: Toronto is one of the most multicultural cities in the world.

stops.name: Tobermory
stops.description: A harbor village of clear water, limestone cliffs, and island ferries.
stops.fact: Tobermory is the northern terminus of the Bruce Trail.

stops.name: South Baymouth
stops.description: The southern gateway to Manitoulin Island beside Lake Huron.
stops.fact: The seasonal Chi-Cheemaun ferry links South Baymouth with Tobermory.

stops.name: Sault Ste. Marie
stops.description: A Great Lakes city beside the rapids joining Superior and Huron.
stops.fact: The Sault locks allow vessels to bypass the St. Marys River rapids.

stops.name: Thunder Bay
stops.description: A Lake Superior port framed by boreal forest and the Sleeping Giant.
stops.fact: Thunder Bay was formed by the merger of Fort William and Port Arthur.

stops.name: Winnipeg
stops.description: Prairie skies and river meeting points.
stops.fact: Winnipeg is known as the Gateway to the West.

stops.name: Regina
stops.description: A prairie capital of broad skies, parks, museums, and civic landmarks.
stops.fact: Regina was named in honor of Queen Victoria.

stops.name: Medicine Hat
stops.description: A sunny prairie city shaped by clay, natural gas, and river coulees.
stops.fact: Medicine Hat became known for industries powered by abundant natural gas.

stops.name: Calgary
stops.description: Foothills, rodeo spirit, and mountain access.
stops.fact: Calgary is close to Banff National Park.

stops.name: Banff
stops.description: A mountain town surrounded by the peaks and lakes of Banff National Park.
stops.fact: Banff National Park was Canada's first national park.

stops.name: Golden
stops.description: A mountain railway town near six Canadian national parks.
stops.fact: Golden stands where the Kicking Horse and Columbia rivers meet.

stops.name: Kelowna
stops.description: An Okanagan Valley city of orchards, vineyards, beaches, and lake views.
stops.fact: Kelowna sits on the eastern shore of Okanagan Lake.

stops.name: Vancouver
stops.description: Finish between ocean, forests, and peaks.
stops.fact: Vancouver has one of North Americas largest urban parks.

title: Thailand Journey
description: Travel Thailand from Bangkok bustle to Phuket beaches.
shortTagline: Temples, old capitals, northern markets, and islands.

stops.name: Bangkok
stops.description: A vibrant start of temples and river boats.
stops.fact: Bangkok has one of the world's longest ceremonial city names.

stops.name: Ayutthaya
stops.description: Ancient ruins and peaceful waterways.
stops.fact: Ayutthaya was once one of the world's largest cities.

stops.name: Lopburi
stops.description: An ancient central Thai city of Khmer ruins and lively temple squares.
stops.fact: Lopburi was an important royal center during the reign of King Narai.

stops.name: Sukhothai
stops.description: Lotus ponds and brick temples preserve Thailand's first great capital.
stops.fact: Sukhothai Historical Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

stops.name: Lampang
stops.description: A northern city of teak houses, ceramics, temples, and horse carriages.
stops.fact: Lampang remains famous for its traditional horse-drawn carriages.

stops.name: Chiang Mai
stops.description: Northern temples, markets, and mountain air.
stops.fact: Chiang Mai has hundreds of Buddhist temples.

stops.name: Surat Thani
stops.description: A southern river city and gateway to the islands of the Gulf of Thailand.
stops.fact: The name Surat Thani means City of Good People.

stops.name: Khao Sok
stops.description: Rainforest cliffs, caves, and jungle trails surround a protected park.
stops.fact: Khao Sok protects one of southern Thailand's largest rainforest landscapes.

stops.name: Phang Nga
stops.description: A limestone landscape of caves, mangroves, islands, and sheltered bays.
stops.fact: Phang Nga Bay is known for steep limestone karst towers.

stops.name: Krabi
stops.description: A coastal gateway of limestone cliffs, mangroves, beaches, and island ferries.
stops.fact: Krabi Province includes more than one hundred islands in the Andaman Sea.

stops.name: Phi Phi Islands
stops.description: Dramatic limestone islands rise from clear Andaman waters between Krabi and Phuket.
stops.fact: Ko Phi Phi Don is the only permanently inhabited island in the Phi Phi group.

stops.name: Phuket
stops.description: A tropical finish near beaches and islands.
stops.fact: Phuket is Thailands largest island.

title: Around the World Lite
description: Touch six world regions in one long virtual journey.
shortTagline: A compact world tour across iconic global stops.

stops.name: London
stops.description: Begin with a global city and royal parks.
stops.fact: London is home to speakers of more than 300 languages.

stops.name: Dover
stops.description: White cliffs and a great castle guard the narrow English Channel.
stops.fact: Dover has served as a gateway between Britain and continental Europe for centuries.

stops.name: Calais
stops.description: A French Channel port facing the cliffs of England.
stops.fact: Calais lies near the narrowest part of the English Channel.

stops.name: Paris
stops.description: Bridges, museums, markets, and boulevards mark the first continental capital.
stops.fact: Paris grew around islands and crossings of the Seine.

stops.name: Dijon
stops.description: Burgundy architecture and food traditions fill the historic center.
stops.fact: Dijon was a capital of the powerful medieval Duchy of Burgundy.

stops.name: Lyon
stops.description: A culinary city where the Rhone and Saone rivers meet.
stops.fact: Lyon's old passageways are known as traboules.

stops.name: Geneva
stops.description: An international lakeside city framed by the Alps and Jura.
stops.fact: Geneva hosts the European headquarters of the United Nations.

stops.name: Milan
stops.description: Gothic spires, design, and grand arcades introduce northern Italy.
stops.fact: Milan Cathedral took nearly six centuries to complete.

stops.name: Florence
stops.description: Renaissance art and stone bridges line the Arno River.
stops.fact: Florence was a major center of the Italian Renaissance.

stops.name: Rome
stops.description: Ancient monuments and layered neighborhoods complete the European leg.
stops.fact: Rome contains monuments spanning more than two thousand years.

stops.name: Cairo
stops.description: Step from river streets toward ancient monuments.
stops.fact: The Nile is often considered the world's longest river.

stops.name: Delhi
stops.description: Markets, monuments, and layered history.
stops.fact: Delhi has been rebuilt many times across centuries.

stops.name: Singapore
stops.description: A clean, green city-state stop near the equator.
stops.fact: Singapore has four official languages.

stops.name: Jakarta
stops.description: A vast island capital shaped by trade, canals, and many cultures.
stops.fact: Jakarta developed around the historic port of Sunda Kelapa.

stops.name: Sydney
stops.description: Harbor bridges and ocean light.
stops.fact: Sydney Harbour Bridge opened in 1932.

stops.name: Honolulu
stops.description: A Pacific island capital between volcanic ridges and the sea.
stops.fact: Honolulu is the only US state capital located in Polynesia.

stops.name: San Francisco
stops.description: Finish by hills, fog, and the Golden Gate.
stops.fact: The Golden Gate Bridge was once the world's longest suspension bridge.

title: Kyiv Heritage & Legends
description: Walk through the history and legends of ancient Kyiv.
shortTagline: Golden domes, old streets, and Dnipro views.

stops.name: Golden Gate
stops.description: Begin at the fortified gateway of medieval Kyiv.
stops.fact: The reconstructed gate stands above foundations from the eleventh century.

stops.name: Saint Sophia’s Cathedral
stops.description: Discover mosaics and frescoes at Kyiv’s spiritual heart.
stops.fact: Its surviving mosaics include works created in the eleventh century.

stops.name: Andriyivskyy Descent
stops.description: Follow the storied cobbled street into the old city.
stops.fact: The descent has long connected Upper Kyiv with the Podil district.

stops.name: Podil
stops.description: Explore Kyiv’s historic riverside trading quarter.
stops.fact: Podil was rebuilt on a new street grid after the great fire of 1811.

stops.name: Mariinskyi Park
stops.description: Walk through a leafy park above the Dnipro slopes.
stops.fact: The park adjoins the eighteenth-century Mariinskyi Palace.

stops.name: Kyiv Pechersk Lavra
stops.description: Finish among golden domes and ancient monastic caves.
stops.fact: The monastery was founded in 1051 and became a major Orthodox center.

title: Alpine Peaks & Castles
description: Cross Alpine lakes, peaks, passes, and storybook castles.
shortTagline: Mountain air, blue lakes, and royal fortresses.

stops.name: Neuschwanstein Castle
stops.description: Start beneath Bavaria’s famous fairytale castle.
stops.fact: King Ludwig II commissioned the castle in the nineteenth century.

stops.name: Eibsee
stops.description: Circle a clear mountain lake beneath the Zugspitze.
stops.fact: Eight small islands dot the lake beneath Germany’s highest peak.

stops.name: Zugspitze
stops.description: Reach the dramatic summit ridge of Germany.
stops.fact: The summit rises to 2,962 meters above sea level.

stops.name: Innsbruck Old Town
stops.description: Enter a colorful Alpine city framed by steep peaks.
stops.fact: Its Golden Roof is covered with thousands of gilded copper tiles.

stops.name: Salzburg Alpine Passes
stops.description: Traverse sweeping high roads and mountain viewpoints.
stops.fact: The Grossglockner road crosses one of Austria’s great high passes.

stops.name: Hohensalzburg Fortress
stops.description: Finish above Salzburg at its hilltop fortress.
stops.fact: The fortress is among Europe’s largest preserved medieval castles.

title: Kyoto Autumn Temples
description: Wander through maple colors, bamboo, shrines, and old Kyoto.
shortTagline: Autumn leaves, temple bells, and lantern-lit lanes.

stops.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
stops.description: Begin beneath towering stalks of green bamboo.
stops.fact: The grove’s rustling sound is recognized as a symbolic Japanese soundscape.

stops.name: Kinkaku-ji
stops.description: See the Golden Pavilion reflected in its garden pond.
stops.fact: The upper stories are covered in gold leaf.

stops.name: Ryoan-ji
stops.description: Pause beside one of Japan’s best-known rock gardens.
stops.fact: From any single viewing point, at least one of its fifteen stones is hidden.

stops.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
stops.description: Climb through tunnels of vermilion torii gates.
stops.fact: Thousands of donated gates line the trails of Mount Inari.

stops.name: Gion
stops.description: Walk lantern-lit lanes and traditional wooden streets.
stops.fact: Gion developed as an entertainment district serving nearby shrines.

stops.name: Kiyomizu-dera
stops.description: Finish on a temple terrace above autumn-colored hills.
stops.fact: Its main stage was assembled without nails.

title: Greek Islands Odyssey
description: Island-hop through Minoan ruins, volcanic towns, and Aegean beaches.
shortTagline: Ancient myths, white villages, and blue water.

stops.name: Knossos Palace
stops.description: Begin among the remains of Crete’s Minoan palace.
stops.fact: Knossos is closely linked with the myth of the Minotaur and labyrinth.

stops.name: Samaria Gorge
stops.description: Descend one of Europe’s longest celebrated gorges.
stops.fact: The trail passes through the narrow rock walls known as the Gates.

stops.name: Fira
stops.description: Climb whitewashed lanes along Santorini’s caldera.
stops.fact: Fira sits high on cliffs formed by ancient volcanic eruptions.

stops.name: Oia
stops.description: Follow blue domes toward a famous Aegean sunset.
stops.fact: Oia’s cave houses were carved into volcanic rock.

stops.name: Delos
stops.description: Explore a sacred island of temples and ancient streets.
stops.fact: In Greek mythology, Delos was the birthplace of Apollo and Artemis.

stops.name: Mykonos Beaches
stops.description: Finish beside bright coves and clear Cycladic water.
stops.fact: Mykonos is nicknamed the Island of the Winds.

title: Iceland Ring Road
description: Trace Iceland’s waterfalls, black beaches, ice, and geothermal north.
shortTagline: Waterfalls, glaciers, volcanoes, and northern light.

stops.name: Golden Circle
stops.description: Begin among rift valleys, geysers, and powerful falls.
stops.fact: Thingvellir lies where the North American and Eurasian plates diverge.

stops.name: Skogafoss
stops.description: Approach a broad curtain of water on the south coast.
stops.fact: On sunny days the spray often creates a double rainbow.

stops.name: Reynisfjara Black Beach
stops.description: Walk beside basalt columns and roaring Atlantic surf.
stops.fact: The offshore Reynisdrangar stacks feature in Icelandic troll legends.

stops.name: Jokulsarlon Glacier Lagoon
stops.description: Pass blue icebergs drifting toward the ocean.
stops.fact: The lagoon has expanded as the Breidamerkurjokull glacier retreats.

stops.name: Dettifoss
stops.description: Feel the force of a vast glacial waterfall.
stops.fact: Dettifoss is one of Europe’s most powerful waterfalls by water flow.

stops.name: Lake Myvatn
stops.description: Finish amid lava fields, crater lakes, and geothermal steam.
stops.fact: The lake’s name refers to the abundant midges that support its birdlife.

title: Bali Tropical Trail
description: Cross rice terraces, waterfalls, temples, and volcanic landscapes.
shortTagline: Tropical paths, sacred temples, and green terraces.

stops.name: Ubud Monkey Forest
stops.description: Begin beneath a dense canopy of banyan trees and temples.
stops.fact: The sanctuary protects three temple complexes and hundreds of macaques.

stops.name: Tegallalang Rice Terraces
stops.description: Follow green contours shaped by traditional irrigation.
stops.fact: The terraces use Bali’s cooperative subak water-management system.

stops.name: Tegenungan Waterfall
stops.description: Descend through tropical forest to a powerful cascade.
stops.fact: Unlike many Balinese waterfalls, Tegenungan is not in the high mountains.

stops.name: Mount Batur
stops.description: Climb toward sunrise above a volcanic caldera.
stops.fact: Mount Batur remains an active volcano within a larger ancient caldera.

stops.name: Tanah Lot
stops.description: Reach a sea temple perched on a wave-cut rock.
stops.fact: At high tide the temple appears separated from the mainland.

stops.name: Uluwatu Temple
stops.description: Finish on cliffs above the Indian Ocean.
stops.fact: The temple stands roughly seventy meters above the sea.

title: Scandinavian Fjords & Coast
description: Follow Norway’s colorful ports, deep fjords, cliffs, and ocean roads.
shortTagline: Deep fjords, high cliffs, and wild ocean roads.

stops.name: Bergen Bryggen
stops.description: Begin among colorful timber warehouses by the harbor.
stops.fact: Bryggen preserves the legacy of Bergen’s Hanseatic trading era.

stops.name: Trolltunga
stops.description: Reach a rock ledge suspended above Ringedalsvatnet.
stops.fact: The ledge was shaped by glacial erosion thousands of years ago.

stops.name: Geirangerfjord
stops.description: Move between steep green walls and ribbon waterfalls.
stops.fact: Geirangerfjord forms part of a UNESCO-listed fjord landscape.

stops.name: Alesund
stops.description: Walk through an Art Nouveau town scattered across islands.
stops.fact: Alesund was rebuilt in a unified Jugendstil style after a 1904 fire.

stops.name: Atlantic Ocean Road
stops.description: Cross bridges that curve between skerries and open sea.
stops.fact: The road links small islands with eight distinctive bridges.

stops.name: Trollstigen
stops.description: Finish above a serpentine mountain road and valley.
stops.fact: Trollstigen climbs through eleven dramatic hairpin bends.

title: Prague & Bohemian Castles
description: Journey from Prague’s medieval heart to Bohemia’s castle towns.
shortTagline: Stone bridges, royal castles, and old town squares.

stops.name: Old Town Square Prague
stops.description: Begin beneath Gothic spires and the astronomical clock.
stops.fact: The square has served as Prague’s civic center for centuries.

stops.name: Charles Bridge
stops.description: Cross the Vltava between statues and old towers.
stops.fact: The bridge’s foundation stone was laid in 1357.

stops.name: Prague Castle
stops.description: Climb into a vast complex of palaces and courtyards.
stops.fact: Prague Castle has been a seat of rulers for more than a millennium.

stops.name: Karlstejn Castle
stops.description: Approach a hilltop fortress built for imperial treasures.
stops.fact: Charles IV founded the castle in 1348.

stops.name: Kutna Hora
stops.description: Explore a silver-mining town of cathedrals and stone lanes.
stops.fact: Its medieval silver mines helped finance the Bohemian kingdom.

stops.name: Cesky Krumlov Castle
stops.description: Finish above a winding river and red-roofed old town.
stops.fact: The castle complex includes a rare preserved Baroque theater.

title: Patagonia Wilderness
description: Cross glacier country, granite peaks, lakes, and windswept wilderness.
shortTagline: Granite towers, blue ice, and untamed horizons.

stops.name: Bariloche Lake District
stops.description: Begin among blue lakes and forested Andean ridges.
stops.fact: Bariloche sits within Argentina’s oldest national park.

stops.name: Mount Fitz Roy
stops.description: Approach sharp granite towers above El Chalten.
stops.fact: Fitz Roy’s Tehuelche name, Chalten, means smoking mountain.

stops.name: Perito Moreno Glacier
stops.description: Walk beside a wall of blue ice advancing into the lake.
stops.fact: The glacier is famous for periodic ice-bridge ruptures.

stops.name: Torres del Paine
stops.description: Enter a park of granite towers, steppe, and turquoise lakes.
stops.fact: The three granite towers are among Patagonia’s defining landmarks.

stops.name: Grey Glacier
stops.description: Follow floating ice toward the Southern Patagonian Ice Field.
stops.fact: Grey Glacier is part of one of the largest ice fields outside the polar regions.

stops.name: Tierra del Fuego
stops.description: Finish where forested mountains meet the Beagle Channel.
stops.fact: The archipelago’s name dates to fires observed by early European sailors.

title: Scottish Highlands & Lochs
description: Follow Highland glens, legendary lochs, castles, and island cliffs.
shortTagline: Misty glens, ancient castles, and legendary lochs.

stops.name: Edinburgh Castle
stops.description: Begin at the fortress above Scotland’s capital.
stops.fact: The castle rock is the remnant of an extinct volcano.

stops.name: Glencoe
stops.description: Enter a steep-sided glen shaped by glaciers and history.
stops.fact: Glencoe’s landscape formed from ancient volcanic activity and ice.

stops.name: Glenfinnan Viaduct
stops.description: Cross a sweeping railway viaduct above a green valley.
stops.fact: Its twenty-one arches were completed at the end of the nineteenth century.

stops.name: Loch Ness
stops.description: Trace the dark water of Scotland’s most legendary loch.
stops.fact: Loch Ness contains more water than all the lakes of England and Wales combined.

stops.name: Eilean Donan Castle
stops.description: Reach an island castle where three sea lochs meet.
stops.fact: The restored castle stands on foundations first fortified in the thirteenth century.

stops.name: Isle of Skye
stops.description: Finish among sea cliffs, pinnacles, and misty ridges.
stops.fact: Skye’s dramatic Cuillin mountains include twelve Munros.

title: First Journey: London
description: Build your walking habit on a short route across central London.
shortTagline: Five landmarks and your first 15 km adventure.

stops.name: Westminster
stops.description: Begin beside Big Ben and the Houses of Parliament.
stops.fact: The Elizabeth Tower is commonly known by the name of its great bell, Big Ben.

stops.name: Buckingham Palace
stops.description: Reach the royal residence through St James’s Park.
stops.fact: The palace has served as the official London residence of the sovereign since 1837.

stops.name: Hyde Park
stops.description: Walk through one of London’s largest green spaces.
stops.fact: Hyde Park began as a royal hunting ground in the sixteenth century.

stops.name: British Museum
stops.description: Explore a landmark dedicated to human history and culture.
stops.fact: The museum opened to the public in 1759.

stops.name: Tower Bridge
stops.description: Finish above the Thames at London’s iconic bascule bridge.
stops.fact: Tower Bridge opened in 1894 and still raises for river traffic.

title: First Journey: New York
description: Build your walking habit on a short route through New York.
shortTagline: Five landmarks and your first 15 km adventure.

stops.name: Times Square
stops.description: Begin among the lights and theaters of Times Square.
stops.fact: Times Square was renamed in 1904 after The New York Times moved nearby.

stops.name: Empire State Building
stops.description: Reach one of the world’s most recognizable skyscrapers.
stops.fact: The Empire State Building opened in 1931.

stops.name: High Line
stops.description: Follow an elevated park above Manhattan streets.
stops.fact: The High Line was created on a former freight railway.

stops.name: One World Trade Center
stops.description: Walk south to the landmark rising above Lower Manhattan.
stops.fact: Its architectural height is 1,776 feet.

stops.name: Brooklyn Bridge
stops.description: Finish above the East River on the historic bridge.
stops.fact: Brooklyn Bridge opened in 1883.

title: First Journey: Tokyo
description: Build your walking habit on a short route through Tokyo.
shortTagline: Five landmarks and your first 16 km adventure.

stops.name: Shibuya Crossing
stops.description: Begin at Tokyo’s famous pedestrian crossing.
stops.fact: Thousands of people can cross here during the busiest periods.

stops.name: Meiji Shrine
stops.description: Enter a forested shrine in the heart of the city.
stops.fact: The shrine is dedicated to Emperor Meiji and Empress Shoken.

stops.name: Shinjuku Gyoen
stops.description: Walk through broad lawns and traditional gardens.
stops.fact: The park combines Japanese, English, and French garden styles.

stops.name: Imperial Palace
stops.description: Reach the moats and gardens of the Imperial Palace.
stops.fact: The palace stands on the former site of Edo Castle.

stops.name: Senso-ji
stops.description: Finish at Tokyo’s oldest Buddhist temple.
stops.fact: Senso-ji traces its history to the seventh century.

title: First Journey: Cairo
description: Build your walking habit on a short route through Cairo.
shortTagline: Five landmarks and your first 15 km adventure.

stops.name: Egyptian Museum
stops.description: Begin beside a landmark collection of ancient Egyptian history.
stops.fact: The museum opened in its Tahrir Square building in 1902.

stops.name: Cairo Tower
stops.description: Reach the tower overlooking the Nile and the city.
stops.fact: The lattice design was inspired by the lotus plant.

stops.name: Al-Azhar Mosque
stops.description: Continue into historic Islamic Cairo.
stops.fact: Al-Azhar was founded in the tenth century.

stops.name: Cairo Citadel
stops.description: Climb toward the medieval fortress above Cairo.
stops.fact: Saladin began building the citadel in the twelfth century.

stops.name: Khan el-Khalili
stops.description: Finish among the lanes and markets of the historic bazaar.
stops.fact: The market district dates back to the fourteenth century.

title: First Journey: Rio
description: Build your walking habit on a short route through Rio de Janeiro.
shortTagline: Five landmarks and your first 18 km adventure.

stops.name: Copacabana Beach
stops.description: Begin beside the Atlantic on Copacabana’s famous promenade.
stops.fact: The promenade is known for its black-and-white wave mosaic.

stops.name: Ipanema Beach
stops.description: Follow the coast toward Ipanema and its mountain views.
stops.fact: Ipanema became internationally famous through a bossa nova song.

stops.name: Rodrigo de Freitas Lagoon
stops.description: Circle a lagoon framed by Rio’s hills.
stops.fact: The lagoon hosted rowing events during the 2016 Olympic Games.

stops.name: Rio Botanical Garden
stops.description: Walk beneath palms in Rio’s historic botanical garden.
stops.fact: The garden was founded in 1808.

stops.name: Christ the Redeemer
stops.description: Finish on Corcovado beneath Rio’s iconic statue.
stops.fact: Christ the Redeemer was completed in 1931.
